title: Carrier support can “save your number”
scenario: A caller claiming to be your mobile carrier says someone requested a SIM transfer. They can cancel it if you tell them the security PIN sent by text within five minutes.

answers.A: Log in yourself and change the account PIN/password before contacting support.
answers.B: Read the PIN because preventing a SIM swap is time-sensitive and the caller is offering to stop it.
answers.C: End the call and contact the carrier through its official app, site or known support number to secure the account.

explanation: The code may be exactly what an attacker needs to complete a SIM swap. Secure the account from a channel you control.
proTip: Do not hand the “stop the attack” caller the code that completes the attack.
